```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.bg = "white", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 144, fig.align = "center")
library(potentiomap)
library(terra)
data("synthetic_wells", package = "potentiomap")
```

The package standardizes groundwater head in `Z` and observation names in
`Name`. Keep horizontal units, head units, measuring-point corrections, and the
vertical datum explicit in project metadata. The synthetic examples do not
claim a field vertical datum.

## Direct groundwater-elevation measurements

```{r direct-head}
direct <- ps_make_points(
  synthetic_wells,
  x = "x", y = "y",
  value = "gw_elevation",
  name_col = "well_id",
  crs = "EPSG:26916"
)
head(values(direct)[, c("well_id", "gw_elevation", "Name", "Z")])
```

## Positive depth to water plus a DEM

`ps_potentiometric_points()` applies:

\[
\text{groundwater elevation} = \text{land-surface elevation} - \text{depth to water}.
\]

Positive depth means below land surface. A negative value describes head above
land surface, but users should verify that convention in the source record.

<figure class="figure">
  <img src="../depth-to-water-cross-section.png"
       class="figure-img img-fluid"
       alt="Groundwater cross-section on a white background. A sloping land surface lies above a horizontal groundwater surface and documented vertical datum. Double-ended dimension arrows show land-surface elevation from datum to land, positive depth to water measured downward from land to groundwater, and groundwater elevation from datum to groundwater. The equation states groundwater elevation equals land-surface elevation minus depth to water.">
</figure>

```{r dem-pathway}
data("synthetic_dem", package = "potentiomap")
from_dem <- ps_potentiometric_points(
  synthetic_wells,
  x = "x", y = "y",
  depth_col = "depth_to_water",
  surface = synthetic_dem,
  name_col = "well_id",
  crs = "EPSG:26916"
)
head(values(from_dem)[, c("Name", "surface_elevation", "depth_to_water", "Z")])
```

The raster and wells must represent compatible horizontal coordinates. Surface
elevation and depth to water must use the same vertical units.

## Depth to water plus an elevation column

```{r column-pathway}
from_column <- ps_potentiometric_points(
  synthetic_wells,
  x = "x", y = "y",
  depth_col = "depth_to_water",
  surface_col = "surface_elevation",
  name_col = "well_id",
  crs = "EPSG:26916"
)
head(values(from_column)[, c("Name", "surface_elevation", "depth_to_water", "Z")])
```

## Depth to water plus separate surface-elevation points

Separate surface observations are matched by name when possible; otherwise the
released function interpolates surface elevation to the depth points with IDW.

```{r separate-surface}
data("synthetic_surface_points", package = "potentiomap")
from_separate <- ps_potentiometric_points(
  synthetic_wells,
  x = "x", y = "y",
  depth_col = "depth_to_water",
  surface = synthetic_surface_points,
  surface_col = "surface_elevation",
  name_col = "well_id",
  surface_name_col = "point_id",
  crs = "EPSG:26916",
  idw_power = 2
)
head(values(from_separate)[, c("Name", "surface_elevation", "depth_to_water", "Z")])
```

This pathway adds a surface-interpolation assumption. Record the source-point
network and do not treat the calculated elevation as more precise than its
inputs.

## Data frame, sf, and terra inputs

```{r sf-input}
wells_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(synthetic_wells, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 26916)
from_sf <- ps_make_points(
  wells_sf,
  value = "gw_elevation",
  name_col = "well_id"
)
c(class = class(from_sf)[1], crs = crs(from_sf, proj = TRUE), rows = nrow(from_sf))
```

```{r terra-input}
wells_vect <- vect(synthetic_wells, geom = c("x", "y"), crs = "EPSG:26916")
from_terra <- ps_make_points(
  wells_vect,
  value = "gw_elevation",
  name_col = "well_id"
)
head(values(from_terra)[, c("Name", "Z")])
```

```{r pathway-check}
data.frame(
  pathway = c("direct head", "depth + DEM", "depth + column", "depth + separate points", "sf", "terra"),
  observations = c(nrow(direct), nrow(from_dem), nrow(from_column), nrow(from_separate), nrow(from_sf), nrow(from_terra)),
  finite_Z = c(sum(is.finite(values(direct)$Z)), sum(is.finite(values(from_dem)$Z)),
               sum(is.finite(values(from_column)$Z)), sum(is.finite(values(from_separate)$Z)),
               sum(is.finite(values(from_sf)$Z)), sum(is.finite(values(from_terra)$Z)) )
)
```

Assigning a CRS declares what coordinates already mean; transforming a CRS
recalculates coordinates. See [input formats and coordinate systems](input-formats-crs.html)
before interpolating field observations.
